title: What Happens If You Break Your Knuckle?
sources: Cleveland Clinic, 'Boxer's Fracture' (break of the fifth metacarpal neck, usually from punching a hard object; swelling, bruising, a sunken or missing knuckle; treated with a splint or cast, sometimes surgery; heals in about 6 weeks)
AAOS OrthoInfo, 'Hand Fractures' (knuckles are the heads of the metacarpal bones; diagnosed with X-ray; bone heals by forming new bone (callus) across the break)

lines.text: What happens if you break your knuckle?
Well, it usually happens when you punch something hard,
like a wall, and the wall always wins.
Your knuckles are the ends of the long bones in your hand,
and the pinky one cracks so often that doctors call it a boxer's fracture.
Within minutes, your hand swells up like a balloon,
and that knuckle can actually sink in and disappear.
A doctor's X-ray shows the crack,
then a splint holds the bone still for about six weeks,
while your body builds brand new bone right over the break.
lines.caps: WHILE YOUR *BODY | BUILDS NEW *BONE | OVER THE *BREAK

lines.text: So next time you want to punch a wall, maybe don't.
